title: Sign out
heading: Sign out
inventory.holding: Everything this service is still holding for {username}, across every protocol family it speaks.
inventory.globalNote: The default. A POST to /logout with nothing selected does exactly this.
inventory.selectedNote: Tick them in the tables below. Nothing ticked ends nothing.
inventory.liveCount: {total} live item(s) in {families, plural, one {# family} other {# families}}. Some of them cannot be ended by anybody — they are listed with the reason, because a sign-out that hid them would look complete when it is not.
inventory.anyUserOpen: This service checks no password anywhere, so ?username= names anybody and grants nothing that was not already true — signing in as them takes one request. logout.anyUser turns that off.
inventory.anyUserOff: logout.anyUser is off, so this endpoint acts only on the session you are holding.
inventory.productMode: This service is in product mode, so this endpoint acts only on the session you are holding.
inventory.operatorView: The operator's view of the same lists, with an undo, is /admin/logout.
family.notListed: {count} more not listed (logout.maxRows is {held} held against a cap). A GLOBAL logout still ends every one of them — the cap is on what is drawn, never on what a termination reaches.
result.title: Signed out
result.headingSelected: Signed out of what was ticked
result.nothingEnded: Nothing was ended. Either nothing was live, or everything ticked had already gone.
result.notEndedNote: These are the honest half. Most of them cannot be ended by anybody: nothing consults this service when an assertion, a service ticket or an SVID is presented, so there is no revocation to perform.
result.nothingLeft: Nothing. This service is holding no live session or credential for {key} that it can still see.
